claims: SU(2) spin coherent states stereographically parametrized by azimuth phi and projection variable x = I cos(theta) canonically map the frozen-alignment PRM Hamiltonian onto a classical energy function on the sphere with Poisson bracket {phi, x} = 1.

Stationary points of H(x, phi) track the average angular momentum orientation, exhibiting pitchfork bifurcation from planar to aplanar rotation at a critical angular momentum depending on triaxiality gamma and tilting angles alpha, alpha'.

Quantization along the minimal energy path phi_0(x) yields a 1D Schroedinger equation with coordinate-dependent effective mass B(x) = [d^2 H/d phi^2]^(-1) and potential V(x) reproducing double-well tunneling.

Tilted-axis wobbling provides a continuous physical transition between transverse and longitudinal wobbling: non-zero particle tilting shifts the wobbling energy minimum to lower spins, naturally explaining the increasing Delta E(I) in 133La without abandoning particle alignment.

Non-vanishing and asymmetric tilting of quasiparticle spins (e.g., alpha'=8 deg in 138Pm) breaks the high-spin chiral degeneracy, reproducing the parabolic rebound of Delta E(I) and in-band B(M1)/B(E2) ratios.

boundary: Rigid frozen alignment (FA) replaces dynamic quasiparticle operators by constant vectors and neglects rotation-induced pair-breaking
Harmonic expansion in phi assumes localized fluctuations around phi_0(x) and is less accurate near shallow isotropic saddle points
Model parameters (gamma, J_0, alpha, alpha') are phenomenological and must be constrained by independent microscopic PES and lifetime measurements
